review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Hawks came in with a league-average attack and a 5% leakier than average defense (4-9, 95.5 scored and 103.8 allowed a game over 13 games), worth about 25 and 25 games of evidence. Projected to score 94, they scored 120 (+26 points, 28% over); projected to allow 103.3, they allowed 110 (+6.7 points, 7% over).

Phoenix came in with a 2% above average attack and a league-average defense (4-7, 97.1 scored and 95.7 allowed a game over 11 games), worth about 23 and 23 games of evidence. Projected to score 103.3, they scored 110 (+6.7 points, 7% over); projected to allow 94, they allowed 120 (+26 points, 28% over).

The bigger miss was Hawks' scoring (+26 points against projection); both sides outscored their projections, so the game ran hotter than either team's numbers said.

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 230 against 197.3 projected (+32.7), about the 98th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±16).

Margin: Hawks by 10 against Phoenix by 9.3 projected, about the 5th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±12).

An outlier: the simulations had a result this far off less than about 5% of the time, which usually means an input was wrong or missing, not just bad luck.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×1.166 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -20 points. It counts toward Hoops+ scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 27 graded Hoops+ games the algo now scales scoring ×1.002 and gives home teams -0.9 points. Team corrections start after 3 graded games for a team.

review.body: Wrong side, total outside its normal range, margin outside its normal range (off by 19.3 points), no bet.
